title: Fisher-weighted Mirror code composition
hypothesis: Fisher-weighted composition in a shared task-delta basis can approximate full-parameter Fisher merging across multiple merge requests with less complete stored state than independent dense deltas, and can improve on unweighted code averaging.
physical_object: shared base model and one rank-8 task-delta basis
mirror_coordinate: merged task-code vector solved from projected per-task diagonal Fisher metrics
logical_multiplicity: 16 distinct multi-task merge requests over 8 source task deltas
controls: native projected-Fisher code solve with identical basis and coefficients

development.selection_metric: mean Fisher-weighted quadratic validation loss, function NRMSE to full Fisher merge, total serialized source-plus-output bytes

paid_objects: source task codes or dense deltas
per-task Fisher diagonals or sufficient statistics

success_gate: Across all audit seeds, Fisher-code merge weighted validation loss <=1.05x full Fisher merge, improves >=10% over unweighted code mean, and complete source-plus-16-output payload <=75% of dense task-delta merge payload. Native identical projected-Fisher implementation is an attribution control; exact alias is FAIL for Mirror-specific value.
failure_gate: Quality, byte or compute gate misses, or native projected-Fisher method matches the Mirror code merge exactly. Report when the basis restriction erases Fisher weighting benefits.
boundaries: Synthetic quadratic task-delta merging only; no pretrained model or natural benchmark.
Fisher diagonals are synthetic log-normal importance weights, not estimated from real task data.
Task Arithmetic and Fisher losses are shared-model merge points, not evidence that task count equals independent capacity.
No GPU/production runtime conclusion; solve and apply costs are analytic proxies.
